issues.legal_issue: A court deciding an eviction claim based on the landlord’s reasonable requirement must consider partial eviction even when the tenant has not specifically pleaded for it.
material_facts: The eviction claim was based on the landlord’s reasonable requirement.
Neither the trial court nor the first appellate court considered on the merits whether eviction from only part of the premises could substantially satisfy that requirement.
The lower courts did not take evidence on partial eviction because there had been no specific pleading on the point.
issues.conclusion: The statutory proviso required the court to determine, after giving both sides an opportunity to lead evidence, whether partial eviction would substantially satisfy the landlord’s reasonable requirement. The absence of a specific pleading did not excuse that inquiry, so the matter was remanded for the first appellate court to decide it.
issues.legal_principle: The second proviso to the Explanation to section 11(1)(h) of the Jammu and Kashmir Houses and Shops Rent Control Act, 1966 requires the court to consider whether partial eviction should be ordered or the entire premises vacated. The court must make that determination after hearing evidence from both sides, and the duty applies even without a specific pleading. R. S. Madan v. G. M. Sadiq, 1971 J&K Law Reports 260, was overruled.

predicates.landlord_need_eviction_case: The landlord sought eviction on the basis of a reasonable requirement of the premises.
predicates.partial_eviction_feasibility_unexamined: The courts had not assessed, after hearing evidence, whether eviction from part of the premises could substantially satisfy the landlord’s requirement.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks eviction for reasonable requirements and the possibility of partial eviction has not been assessed after evidence, the court must determine that possibility after hearing evidence.
